record.original_question: Does every closed manifold of dimension at least 2 admit either a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric whose geodesic flow is ergodic?

evidence.quote: Does every closed manifold (with dimension ≥ 2) admit a metric (Riemannian or Finsler) with ergodic geodesic flow?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold of dimension at least $2$. A Riemannian metric on $M$ is a smooth choice of inner product on each tangent space; a Finsler metric on $M$ is a smooth assignment of a Minkowski norm on each tangent space (a fiberwise smooth, positively homogeneous, strongly convex norm). Either type of metric induces a geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle $SM$, which preserves a canonical smooth measure (the Liouville measure for Riemannian metrics, or its analogue for Finsler metrics). The flow is called ergodic if every flow-invariant measurable subset of $SM$ has either zero or full measure with respect to this canonical measure.

Question: Does every closed smooth manifold of dimension at least $2$ admit either a Riemannian metric or a Finsler metric whose geodesic flow is ergodic?
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in published lists of open problems on geodesics (Burns–Matveev) and is widely regarded as open. While ergodicity of the geodesic flow is established in many special cases (e.g., negatively curved manifolds, Weil–Petersson metric on moduli space, certain non-positively curved or rank-one manifolds), no general construction is known producing an ergodic Riemannian or Finsler metric on every closed manifold of dimension ≥ 2.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and questions about geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Compiled list of open problems on geodesics, including questions about existence of metrics with ergodic geodesic flow.
status_evidence.claim: The question of whether every closed manifold of dimension ≥ 2 admits a Riemannian or Finsler metric with ergodic geodesic flow is listed among open problems on geodesics.

status_evidence.title: The Weil-Petersson geodesic flow is ergodic (Burns, Masur, Wilkinson)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes ergodicity of the Weil–Petersson geodesic flow on moduli space, an example of a setting where ergodicity of geodesic flow is proved.
status_evidence.claim: Ergodicity of geodesic flows is established in particular geometric settings but no general construction covers all closed manifolds of dimension ≥ 2.
